headline: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and oil gained more than 1 percent in early Asian trade on 28 September, with Brent up 1.8 percent to 106.31 dollars and WTI up 1.3 percent to 93.62 dollars, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures slipped about 0.3 percent.

summary.us: The S&P 500 rose 0.51 percent to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.48 percent to 27,068.72 on Friday 25 September, the first winning week in three, after a cooldown in oil eased the pressure from a bond selloff that took the 10 year Treasury yield to 5.184 percent and the 30 year to its highest since 2004. Microsoft did most of the lifting, up 3.66 percent on a Copilot revamp with a coding tool and an always-on agent plus a Stifel upgrade, while Meta fell 3.33 percent as Goldman Sachs turned more cautious and a researcher disclosed a flaw in the Muse agent.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed up 0.34 percent at 23,140.50 and Bank Nifty 0.26 percent at 55,580.40 on 25 September as falling oil helped, but the index still logged a seventh straight weekly loss, down 5.8 percent or 1,430 points over that run and its longest weekly losing streak since the February to March 2020 fall. Foreign institutions sold 3,693.93 crore rupees of cash equities against domestic buying of 2,838.17 crore, the rupee firmed 0.37 percent to 95.80 per dollar, and the IRDAI distribution paper kept re-pricing listed insurance distributors, with PB Fintech down 33.1 percent on the week.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 gained 1.30 percent on 25 September for a fifth straight advance, still digesting the Bank of Japan's 18 September hike to 1.25 percent, a 31 year high, while Hong Kong fell 1.01 percent and both the DAX and FTSE 100 closed lower as oil and yields drove trade. Gold fell 1.53 percent to 4,255.30 and silver 1.82 percent to 63.08 as the dollar index reached a near two month high, and the Brent print captured here reflects Sunday's slide below 100 dollars on truce talk before Trump's rejection sent it back toward 106.

calendar.what: Markets price Trump's rejection of Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with oil up over 1 percent in early Asian trade; SRIT India and Shah Investor's Home IPOs open in India; Moneyview and A-One Steels India IPOs close

Monthly Nifty, Bank Nifty and stock derivatives expiry on NSE; US pending home sales and the Dallas Fed manufacturing index; Acevector, German Green Steel and Power, Runwal Enterprises and Orient Cables IPOs close in India; Carnival and CarMax report

US JOLTS job openings for August, consensus 7.23 million after 7.27 million in July, plus Chicago PMI and Conference Board consumer confidence; China official PMIs; Vishal Nirmiti and Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPOs open and SRIT India and Shah Investor's Home close in India; Oura expected to price and list on Nasdaq; Micron reports

US August PCE price index, the third estimate of Q2 GDP with BEA annual revisions, and ISM manufacturing PMI with consensus 54.8 after 54.6; flash inflation prints from the larger euro area economies; Nike and Accenture report

US September employment report from the BLS at 8:30 am ET, the last major labour reading before the 28 October FOMC, plus initial jobless claims, Challenger job cuts and factory orders; NSE and BSE closed for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti

RBI Monetary Policy Committee begins its three day meeting, 5 to 7 October, with the repo rate at 5.25 percent after four holds and economists split between a 25 basis point hike now and waiting until December; Vishal Nirmiti and Nityas Gems and Jewellery IPOs close

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms all week: the US 10 year Treasury yield reached 5.2251 percent on 24 September, its highest since June 2007, and the 30 year touched 5.47 percent, a 22 year high, on strong manufacturing surveys, hawkish Fed commentary and a poorly bid five year auction, which pushed the dollar index to a two month high. Equities absorbed it anyway, because a reported phased US and Iran arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz took WTI down 7.84 percent on the week and because Meta's Muse AI agent kept re-rating the largest index weights, lifting Meta 12.9 percent over five sessions while knocking bank stocks on 23 September as investors weighed whether agents could shop deposit rates on a customer's behalf. India went the other way, undone by a domestic regulator rather than by yields, after the IRDAI consultation paper on insurance distribution economics proposed commission caps and a five year glide path on expenses of management, taking PB Fintech down 33.1 percent on the week and dragging Nifty 50 to a 0.88 percent weekly loss even after Friday's rebound. Precious metals broke their run, with gold off 2.36 percent and silver off 2.77 percent on the week as real yields and the dollar bit, though both recovered on Friday, and copper held a 2.48 percent weekly gain near its 22 September record; crypto diverged from that risk-off tone, with bitcoin adding 3.38 percent and capital rotating into compute and DeFi tokens even after the Bitget hack. Next week the macro calendar is a labour market week rather than an inflation one, with JOLTS on 30 September, ADP and ISM manufacturing on 1 October and jobless claims and factory orders on 2 October, before the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meets 5 to 7 October with the repo rate at 5.25 percent after four pauses.
